# Task 1: convergence exception, then escalation on the next FIX_FIRST

## 1. Decide the transition

| Observation | Rule | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Re-review `FIX_FIRST`, `TRAJECTORY: CONVERGING (3 -> 1, max severity Moderate)`, `failed[1] == 2`, `converged[1]` unset | The line lacks `max severity Critical`, so the convergence exception applies | Set `converged[1]`. Run one extra ordinary repair, then a re-review. Pass no `model:`. |
| Comparison case: the same line reads `max severity Critical` | No convergence exception | Escalate immediately (step 7 below). |
| Next re-review is `FIX_FIRST` again, even if `CONVERGING` | "A further `FIX_FIRST` escalates whatever the trajectory" | Set `escalated[1]`. Run the escalated round with `model: <implModel>`. |

Tasks 1 and 2 stay `in_progress`, with no tracker calls. `WAVE_BASE_SHA` stays `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`. The round cap is at most `4 + N` re-reviews in this wave. I check it before each re-review dispatch.

## 2. Bounded read of the FIX_FIRST report

I need its findings for the repair payload. This is one read of the printed `report <path>` from the `wave <w> review <k> verdict FIX_FIRST report <path> tree <sha>` line.

```ts
read({ path: "<REPORT_DIR>/wave<w>-review<k>.md", limit: 300 })
```

If this read does not reach the `TRAJECTORY:` footer, I re-dispatch the same wave-reviewer once with `Compact report: findings and footer only, at most 150 lines`. I attribute findings to Task 1 through manifest `files`, or through `touchedTasks`.

## 3. Repair-base snapshot (isolated wave)

<!-- repair-base-shell -->
```bash
RP_ROOT='/workspace/project'
RP_BASE='1111111111111111111111111111111111111111'
RP_DIR=$(mktemp -d) || exit 1
RP_TREE="$RP_DIR/tree"
git -C "$RP_ROOT" add -A || exit 1
git -C "$RP_ROOT" diff --binary --cached "$RP_BASE" > "$RP_DIR/integrated.patch" || exit 1
git -C "$RP_ROOT" worktree add --detach "$RP_TREE" "$RP_BASE" || exit 1
if [ -s "$RP_DIR/integrated.patch" ]; then git -C "$RP_TREE" apply --index "$RP_DIR/integrated.patch" || exit 1; fi
git -C "$RP_TREE" -c user.name=gauntlet -c user.email=gauntlet@local commit -q --allow-empty -m "wave integrated snapshot" || exit 1
printf 'repair-base: %s %s\n' "$RP_TREE" "$(git -C "$RP_TREE" rev-parse HEAD)"
```

If the wave is in-place, skip this step. Dispatch with `cwd: "/workspace/project"`, no `worktree:`, and the wave union as `SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS`.

## 4. Extra ordinary repair carrier

This is a repair dispatch, so it has no `context: "fresh"` and no `model:`.

```ts
subagent({ async: false, cwd: "<RP_TREE from repair-base line>",
  chain: [{ parallel: [
    { agent: "implementer", as: "impl_1", outputSchema: IMPLEMENTER_STATUS_SCHEMA,
      output: "<REPORT_DIR>/wave<w>-repair<k+1>-task1.md", outputMode: "file-only",
      task: `planPath: /workspace/project/doc/plans/feature.md; anchor: ### Task 1:; Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/feature.md; Leg: <owning leg>; Rules: <task 1 Rules> + <leg> Rules from home ## Legs, resolved in the owning checkout; SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: <Task 1 manifest tests, verbatim array elements>.
Findings to fix: <Task 1-attributed findings from the bounded read>
## Previous review report (re-review trigger)
<REPORT_DIR>/wave<w>-review<k>.md
pi-cohort saves your final report; do not write it yourself.` }
  ], worktree: true, concurrency: 4,
     stopOn: { path: "/status", in: ["BLOCKED", "NEEDS_CONTEXT", "DONE_WITH_CONCERNS"] } }]
})
```

## 5. Integrate the repair and run the gate

```bash
test -s "<Artifacts>/worktree-diffs/step-0/task-0-implementer.patch"
git -C /workspace/project apply --index "<Artifacts>/worktree-diffs/step-0/task-0-implementer.patch"
# print: wave <w> repair <k+1> task 1 <status> report <path> delta <path> applied <yes|no>
git -C /workspace/project worktree remove --force "<RP_TREE>"
git -C /workspace/project add -A
git -C /workspace/project diff --stat --cached <tree from the prior review line>
(cd /workspace/project && <Task 1 test i>) > "<REPORT_DIR>/gate-<i>.log" 2>&1; echo "wave <w> gate <i> exit $?"
```

If `diff --stat` is empty, I dispatch no re-review. That counts as a failed attempt and goes to escalation. A red gate also escalates, because `converged[1]` is now spent.

## 6. Record the Fix delta tree and dispatch the re-review

<!-- fix-delta-tree-shell -->
```bash
FD_ROOT='/workspace/project'
FD_INDEX=$(mktemp) || exit 1
cp "$(git -C "$FD_ROOT" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path index)" "$FD_INDEX" || { rm -f "$FD_INDEX"; exit 1; }
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" add -A && GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" write-tree
FD_STATUS=$?
rm -f "$FD_INDEX"
exit "$FD_STATUS"
```

```ts
subagent({ async: false, context: "fresh", cwd: "/workspace/project",
  chain: [{ parallel: [
    { agent: "wave-reviewer", output: "<REPORT_DIR>/wave<w>-review<k+1>.md",
      outputMode: "file-only", outputSchema: WAVE_VERDICT_SCHEMA,
      task: `planPath: /workspace/project/doc/plans/feature.md; anchors: ["### Task 1:", "### Task 2:"]; Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/feature.md; Leg: <owning leg>; Rules: <combined task/leg Rules, resolved in owning checkout>; BASE_SHA: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111; HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE; SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: <wave union of Task 1 + Task 2 manifest tests>
## Previous review report (re-review trigger)
<REPORT_DIR>/wave<w>-review<k>.md
## Fix delta
tree-before: <tree from prior review line>
tree-after: <SHA printed by the block above>
Run git -C /workspace/project diff --binary <tree-before> <tree-after> yourself. Apply the trajectory block.` }
  ], stopOn: { path: "/verdict", in: ["FIX_FIRST", "REJECT"] } }]
})
```

After it returns, I print `wave <w> review <k+1> verdict <value> report <path> tree <sha>`.

## 7. Escalation after the observed second FIX_FIRST CONVERGING

The re-review returns `FIX_FIRST` again. I do one bounded `read` of `<REPORT_DIR>/wave<w>-review<k+1>.md` with `limit: 300` for its findings. Then I print:

```
escalated round for task 1 after 2 failed attempts
```

```ts
gauntlet_setting({ key: "escalationLoop" })
```

Then I rerun the section 3 repair-base block to get a fresh `RP_TREE`. If `implModel` resolves, I dispatch this carrier:

```ts
subagent({ async: false, cwd: "<new RP_TREE>",
  chain: [{ parallel: [
    { agent: "implementer", as: "impl_1", model: "<implModel verbatim>", outputSchema: IMPLEMENTER_STATUS_SCHEMA,
      output: "<REPORT_DIR>/wave<w>-escalated-task1.md", outputMode: "file-only",
      task: `<same payload as section 4, with findings from review<k+1> and its path under ## Previous review report (re-review trigger)>` }
  ], worktree: true, concurrency: 4,
     stopOn: { path: "/status", in: ["BLOCKED", "NEEDS_CONTEXT", "DONE_WITH_CONCERNS"] } }]
})
```

## Stop boundary

I stop here, before any of these results exist:
- The `implModel` value.
- The `escalationLoop` setting.
- The escalated repair status.
- The Task 1 tests.

If `implModel` is undefined or `gauntlet_setting` is unavailable, I emit the stop note (`gauntlet: question`, stopped on task 1) and do no further dispatch.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Both outputs state the exception correctly: one ordinary repair when the line lacks `max severity Critical` and converged[1] is unset, immediate escalation on Critical, and escalation on the next FIX_FIRST regardless of trajectory (After's §1 table and §7 heading make this explicit). After stays on the right side of the fact, but two phrasings are risky. First, §2's compact-report retry is triggered by 'does not reach the `TRAJECTORY:` footer', which a reader could mistake for redispatching the reviewer to recover a trajectory; since the trajectory was already observed in the verdict line, word it as a read-overflow condition ('if the 300-line read truncates before the footer, re-dispatch once for a compact findings+footer report; the trajectory itself is already known from the review line and is never a reason to redispatch'). Second, §5's 'A red gate also escalates, because converged[1] is now spent' is not part of the convergence rule and conflicts with Before's 'red gate means a repair from the gate log, not a review'; keep Before's sentence and let escalation follow only from the re-review verdict or the failed-attempt counter, so the transition table stays the single source of escalation.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Both outputs keep the protocol fact: each has a three-row table that sets converged[1] and grants exactly one extra ordinary repair for Moderate with converged unset, escalates on the next FIX_FIRST regardless of trajectory, and escalates immediately on Critical with no exception; neither redispatches to obtain a missing trajectory (Before says a missing review-tree observation cannot be reconstructed, After explicitly says stop and do not dispatch a delta re-review). After additionally delivers the Change well — bounded direct report read at limit 300, committed repair-base snapshot on the current integrated tree, delta-only apply with worktree removal only after a successful apply, and a named read-only delegate restricted to static source facts. Two small wording cautions for After: the escalated carrier places `model` at the subagent top level while Before placed it on the agent entry, so state which placement the carrier schema expects to avoid readers inferring an invented field; and the escalation row should retain Before's explicit 'increment the attributed failure count' phrasing ('count that failure' is slightly looser) so the escalation condition is unambiguously tied to attributed failures rather than any FIX_FIRST.
